name: Purchase history and loyalty data
plain: A signed in shop knows exactly what the person bought, when, and how much they paid.
meaning: Order records show size, health, family and hobby clues and are the most valuable first party data for retail media networks. Tax law has retailers keep records 3 to 7 years in the US. Shared with ad partners only if permitted.

web.api: Server database linked to account ID; loyalty card number

access.persistence: Typically 3 to 7 years for tax records, longer in marketing data
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings

limits.headline: Can see what you bought, when and for how much, once you are signed in
limits.user_action: You sign in to a shop and place or look up orders.
can: Show past orders with dates and prices
Suggest items based on what you bought
Keep points and loyalty rewards tied to your account
cannot: See your purchases at other shops
See your full card number; stores usually keep only the last four digits
Show your history before you sign in on a new device
Know what you buy in cash or at other stores unless you link a loyalty card
limits.reach_label: Everything you buy from that shop

story.what_it_is: A signed in shop remembers everything you bought, and uses it.
story.for_you: Your orders, returns and loyalty points follow you around the shop. You see it as 'buy again' and 'picked for you', but it also shapes ads and prices.
story.for_makers: It is the most valuable data a shop owns. They use it for recommendations, fraud checks and to sell ad space to brands through retail media networks.

use_cases.example: Amazon recommends items based on past orders and shows ads for similar brands.
A retailer lets brands target people who bought a certain kind of diaper or snack.
A shop flags an order that does not match your past habits as possible fraud.
A grocery app pre fills your usual weekly basket.
An airline uses booking history to offer upgrades and decide your loyalty tier.
A buy now pay later service checks order history when it approves credit.

technical_bounds: Data rights (access, delete) apply in EU and California
Sharing requires disclosure and opt out under CCPA

history.change: CCPA gives California residents right to know and delete purchase data

refs.label: IRS how long to keep records
